notes.meaning: God's people call the whole world to join together in praise. A new song does not just mean fresh music, but singing with a renewed heart after experiencing God's love and mercy in a fresh way. The Lord is not a local deity for just one nation, but the living God over all the earth.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine taught that the old song belongs to selfish earthly desires, while the new song belongs to those who love God under Christ's new commandment.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars connect this new song to Israel's return from exile in Babylon, seeing close ties to the words of Isaiah 42:10.

notes.meaning: Praising God is not an activity reserved only for special feast days, but belongs in every single day. Believers are called to share the good news of his salvation, which means his rescue of sinners. Constantly telling what God has done brings honor to his holy name.

God's people are sent out to tell surrounding nations about his majesty and greatness. They are to speak of his wonders, especially the miracles and works of rescue he has done. Praising God in worship naturally spills over into telling other people about him.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine urged Christians to declare God's honor rather than seeking praise for themselves, and applied this to spreading the church across the whole world.

notes.meaning: The Lord deserves the highest praise because his power and greatness have no end. He is greater than any earthly ruler, angel, or false god worshipped by other nations. Standing before his majesty should fill human hearts with deep, reverent awe.

The gods worshipped by the nations around Israel are totally powerless and empty. They are nothing more than lifeless statues made by human hands. In contrast, the Lord showed he alone is God by creating the vast heavens above.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Following an ancient Greek translation that uses the word demons for idols, Augustine taught that the false gods worshipped by the nations are actually demons.

notes.meaning: Royal splendor and majestic power surround the Lord like garments of light. His sanctuary, the sacred place where his people meet him, is filled with his strength and beauty. Coming into God's presence allows worshippers to see how glorious and good he truly is.

Every family and clan across the globe is invited to turn to the Lord. Ascribing glory and strength to God does not add anything new to him, but simply speaks the truth about who he is. People from all backgrounds are welcomed to recognize his rightful rule.

Giving God glory means paying him the deep honor that belongs to him as Creator. Worshippers are invited to bring a gift of thanks and enter his temple courts. While non-Jewish people were once kept away from the temple, this call welcomes everyone near to God.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine taught that the true offering worshippers must bring into God's courts is a humble, repentant heart rather than pride.

notes.meaning: True worship requires approaching God with pure, humble hearts that reflect his perfect holiness. Coming before his majesty should cause everyone to tremble in holy awe. God's worshippers combine joyful gratitude with a deep respect for his authority.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars translate the phrase as holy attire, picturing worshippers or priests putting on special clean ceremonial clothing before entering God's presence.

notes.meaning: Believers must tell the world the good news that the Lord is the true King. His righteous rule brings solid peace and lasting stability to a world shaken by sin. Because God is in charge, he will lead and govern all people with perfect fairness.

differ.view: Christ's reign began when the gospel went out to the nations, establishing his spiritual kingdom in human hearts.
This reign will be fully established when Christ returns in person to rule over the earth in an earthly kingdom.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Early Christian teachers highlighted an ancient reading of this line, 'the Lord reigned from the wood,' seeing it as a prophecy that Christ rules through his cross.

notes.meaning: The heavens, the earth, and the roaring ocean are invited to erupt in celebration. Creation itself is pictured as joining in praise when the Lord takes his throne. The arrival of God's rule is joyful news for the entire universe.

Even the open fields and wild forest trees are described as shouting and singing with delight. Nature has suffered under the burden of human sin and brokenness, but God's presence brings restoration. All of creation rejoices because its Maker is bringing righteous order back to the earth.

The Lord is coming to judge and govern the earth, which brings great joy to his people. Unlike flawed human leaders, he will rule with absolute justice, faithfulness, and truth. For those who trust in God, his coming is not a reason to be terrified, but a day of rescue and peace.
